description: The Docker Build workflow (.github/workflows/docker-build.yml) declares no concurrency block, so when a pull request receives a newer push, its superseded run keeps going to completion on the stale commit. The five test and lint workflows already cancel superseded pull request runs, so Docker Build is the only check that keeps spending runner minutes on a head that can no longer merge. In a recent five-hour window, Docker Build ran to success on 26 superseded commits, about 40 runner-minutes in total.
goal: Add a concurrency block to .github/workflows/docker-build.yml that cancels a superseded pull_request run and leaves every push to main uncancelled. Group pull request runs by workflow and head branch, and give each push to main its own group keyed by ref and commit SHA, so that queued main pushes are never evicted by a later push. Set cancel-in-progress to true only for pull_request events, matching the other workflows in the directory. Change no job steps, triggers or permissions, and change no other file. The module line budgets (holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json) are frozen: do not edit them or any budget-check script, and keep every touched module within the default 200-line budget.
rationale: The other five CI workflows already use a concurrency group with cancel-in-progress set to the pull_request condition. Docker Build lacks it, so superseded pull request heads run to success while their replacements queue behind them. A group keyed by workflow and head branch for pull requests, and by workflow, ref and SHA for pushes, cancels only stale pull request runs. Keying pushes by SHA stops the single-pending-run eviction that a plain workflow-and-ref group causes on main when cancel-in-progress is false.
acceptance_criteria: .github/workflows/docker-build.yml has a top-level concurrency block whose group is built from github.workflow, github.head_ref for pull_request events, and github.ref plus github.sha for all other events.
cancel-in-progress is the expression github.event_name == 'pull_request', so it is true only for pull_request runs.
No job, step, trigger, permission or environment variable in docker-build.yml changes; the diff is limited to the added concurrency block.
No other file changes, and the module line budgets in holon-config/hygiene/module_budgets.json and the budget-check script are untouched.
The existing workflow-trigger and CI-timing tests under apps/sandbox-executor/tests (test_workflow_triggers.py, test_ci_timing_gate.py, test_ci_bookkeeping_wiring.py) still pass under uv run pytest.
On the pull request, a newer push to the same branch cancels the in-progress Docker Build run, and a push to main is not cancelled by a later main push.
